A. The following practices or acts are hereby declared to be illegal and are prohibited by the Butts County Board of Commissioners:
1. The cutting, removing or in any manner making ineffective any seal, locking bank or lock on an electric, gas or water meter.
2. Restoration of service by any means after service has been terminated for nonpayment, or obtaining electricity, gas or water without making the proper deposit with a utility company or receiving proper authorization from a utility company.
3. Obtaining electricity, gas or water by use of jumper wires, or by any other means which bypass a metering device either partially or completely.
4. Damaging or tampering in any manner with any part of a metering device belonging to a utility company.
5. Changing or altering the normal installed position of a metering device in any fashion which causes the normal accurate recording of utility service received to be altered and inaccurate.
6. Obtaining electricity, gas or water by use of a metering device which is not authorized by a utility company.
7. Interfering with the automatic registration, recording and transmission of electricity, gas or water consumption when readings are recorded and/or transmitted electronically.
8. Fraudulently obtaining, or attempting to obtain, service from a utility company by using a false name or identification.
9. Fraudulently obtaining, or attempting to obtain, service from a utility company by placing the account in the name of someone else after the service has been disconnected for nonpayment or theft of service while the person in whose name the service was in when disconnected is still living at the location of the service.
10. Any other reception of electrical power, gas service or water service without proper authorization from a utility company.
B. Alleged violations of this ordinance shall be tried in the Magistrate Court of Butts County. Any person found guilty of violating any section or part of this ordinance shall be fined a sum not less than $250.00 nor more than $1,000.00 on each count.
C. Any person found violating any section or part of this ordinance will be required to make full restitution to the utility company for the cost of the services obtained in violation of the ordinance, for damage to equipment of a utility company and for all associated costs of the investigation. In calculating the amount of restitution to be paid, the court is authorized to consider the following evidence:
1. The cost of the service received as a result of violating this ordinance shall be computed by the utility company.
2. The cost of any damage to utility equipment shall be based on the actual costs. Costs may be computed and updated annually.
3. Investigative and any associated costs will be computed and updated annually by the utility company.
D. Any person in possession of any premises as owner, occupant, or tenant who is found to have an electric, gas or water meter which has been tampered with or altered in violation of this ordinance or found to be receiving electricity, gas or water as a result of any of the methods described above shall be presumed to have knowingly violated the terms of this ordinance. Such receipt of electricity, gas or water shall be deemed prima facie evidence of an intent to defraud or deprive the utility company of recovering proper charges for payment for such service.
E. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.
F. That the provisions of this ordinance are hereby declared to be severable, and if any section, phrase or provision shall be declared or held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect the remainder of the sections, phrases or provisions.
G. The Butts County Board of Commissioners finds that there is a continuing problem with persons illegally obtaining electricity, gas and water by various means and that this results in a loss of revenue to utility companies and creates a dangerous situation that can result in the loss of life or property. THEREFORE, an emergency is hereby declared to exist and this ordinance being necessary for the preservation of the public peace, health and safety shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage and approval. This ordinance shall be cumulative to O.C.G.A. § 16-7-25, and is enacted pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 16-7-25(c).
H. For purposes of this ordinance, "utility company" shall be defined as any company, electric membership corporation, municipality, or political subdivision engaged in the manufacture or sale of electricity, gas or water.
I. The county's code/law enforcement personnel or any certified peace officer having jurisdiction within Butts County are hereby authorized and directed, upon discovery of any violation of this ordinance, to issue a citation for the violator to appear before the court specified in section B of this ordinance.

(a) General. Any customer desiring to be provided with a new tap, or taps, for water service through the authority's water lines shall make an application for water services in person at the Butts County, et al. Water and Sewer Authority administrative offices in Jackson, Georgia. The owner of the property or structure to be served is responsible for the application. The total for connection to the water system shall be the sum of the Tap Fee or Meter Fee, AND the Capital Recovery Fee, and any required Security Deposit.
(b) Application format. Applications for new water service shall include the following information and items: (a) a full and complete description of the project; (b) a full and complete description of the existing, or proposed, land use and development activity; (c) a statement as to whether the applicant seeks a certification of the Capital Recovery Fee Schedule or a certification of an Individual Fee Determination; and (d) if the applicant seeks a certification of an Individual Fee Determination, an Individual Fee Calculation Study complying with the requirements of section 90-36.g.2 shall be included.
(c) Capital recovery fee certification. Upon application to the authority, any person may apply for and shall receive a certification of the Capital Recovery Fee Schedule or a certification of an Individual Fee Determination.
(1) Timely provision of capital recovery fee schedule. The Administrator shall provide an applicant with a written certification of the Capital Recovery Fee Schedule within five (5) working days after receipt of a completed application. The fee schedule certified by the Administrator shall establish the Capital Recovery Fee Schedule for the proposed development activity for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of certification.
(2) Certification of individual fee determination. The Administrator shall provide the applicant with a written certification of an Individual Fee Determination within thirty (30) days after receipt of a completed application. The Individual Fee Determination certified by the Administrator shall establish the Capital Recovery Fee for the proposed development activity for the one hundred eighty (180) day period immediately following the date of such certification.
(3) Payment required prior to water tap agreement. Any persons required to pay Capital Recovery Fees pursuant to this ordinance shall pay such fees to the authority prior to the execution of an approved water tap agreement unless the authority has previously approved a Private Development Agreement providing for an alternative method of payment.
(e) Line availability. If the water distribution system includes a water line adjacent to, or directly across the road from, the customer's property, and no water line extension is required, service will be provided upon the customer executing the Water Tap Agreement and paying the required fees as addressed in Sec. 90-36. Water service requiring a line extension is addressed in Sec. 90-41.
(f) Installation list. Upon complying with the above stated items, the customer will be placed on the tap/meter installation list, and a work order issued for the connection. The connection will be installed by the authority, or its agent, as soon as practicable thereafter.
1013:
(a) Water connection line. Upon the customer meeting the requirements of Article II, the authority will run a water connection line to the property of the customer. The water connection will include a curb stop valve, meter, meter box. A pressure reducer may be installed on the authority's (street) side of the water meter at the discretion of the authority in those areas where average line pressure exceeds 90 psi.
(b) Site of meter. The authority may install its meter at, or near, the property line, or at the authority's option, on the Customer's property within three (3) feet of the property line.
(c) Initiation of service. When the customer has connected his/her piping to the meter, the authority will inspect the connection for a backflow prevention device and cut-off valve and turn on water service. Under no circumstances shall the customer operate the curb stop valve on the authority's (street) side of the meter.
(d) Right to refuse service. The authority reserves the right to refuse service unless the customer's lines and piping are installed in keeping with the authority's specifications and the regulations of the current plumbing code in Butts County.
(e) Interruptions of service. Under normal conditions, the customer will be notified of any anticipated interruptions of service by the authority.
1014:
(a) Water use. Water furnished by the authority shall be used for consumption by the customer, members of the household, employees and/or visitors only. The customer shall not sell water to any other person or permit any other person to use said water. The customer shall not allow anyone else to connect onto the water system serving the customer. Water shall not be used for irrigation, or other purposes, except when water is available in sufficient quantity without interference with the regular domestic consumption in the area served. Disregard of this rule shall be sufficient cause for refusal and/or discontinuance of service.
(b) Access to meter. Where the meter or meter box is placed on the premises of a customer, a suitable place shall be provided by the customer therefor, which is unobstructed and accessible at all times to the meter reader.
(c) Customer's cut-off valve. The customer shall furnish and maintain a private cut-off valve on the customer's side of the meter within, or immediately adjacent to, the meter box.
(d) Backflow prevention device. The customer's piping and apparatus shall be installed and maintained by the customer at the customer's expense so as to prevent a backflow by use of an approved backflow prevention device. This device should meet the specifications of the authority and in most circumstances may be purchased directly from the authority. Under normal conditions, the backflow prevention device must be located within, or immediately adjacent to, the meter box.
(e) Pressure relief device. The customer shall furnish and maintain an approved pressure relief device on a cold water line on the customer's side of the meter according to the requirements of the adopted plumbing code in Butts County.
(f) Pressure regulation. It is the customer's responsibility to furnish and maintain any device necessary to adjust pressure from the authority's lines to protect the customer's private water lines and appurtenances.
(g) Disconnection of wells.
(1) No physical connection. In order to be received as a customer and entitled to receive water from the authority's water system, all applicants must offer proof that any private wells located on their property are not physically connected to the lines of the authority's water system. All applicants, by becoming customers of the authority, covenant and agree that, so long as they continue to be customers of the authority, they will not permit the connection of any private wells to the authority's water system.
(2) Sealing of certain wells. Where water service is available and continued use of a well is determined to pose a health risk by an Environmental Health Specialist of the Butts County Health Department, all affected property owners must connect to the authority's system. In areas designated on an individual lot by lot basis, all existing wells must be disconnected, filled, sealed and plugged from further use, in accordance with the Georgia Department of Natural Resources and Butts County Board of Health regulations, and no new wells may be bored or drilled.
(h) Requirement to connect. For new construction, the water distribution system of any building in which plumbing fixtures are installed shall be connected to the authority's lines if the building is within two hundred feet (200') of a water main.
1015: Duly authorized agents and employees of the authority shall have access at all hours to the premises of the customer and/or property owner for the purposes of installing and removing the property of the authority, inspecting the authority's facilities, reading and testing meters, and repairing and maintaining the facilities of the authority.
1016:
(a) Water rates. The rate schedule for water use is set by the authority from time to time. The current rate for water use is shown in Appendix C. However, water rates will not increase without thirty (30) days notice to the customer. Notice will be sufficiently given to the customer by a publication of the rate changes at least two (2) times in consecutive weeks in the official newspaper of Butts County prior to the rate increase.
(b) Minimum charge. All customers who pay a connection fee to the authority will be required to pay the minimum monthly charge as set by the authority commencing on the next billing date after the meter is set and water is available for consumption. Customers who are not using water may have their meter declared inactive to avoid payment of the minimum charge each month, but will be required to pay a re-activation fee as per section 90-37.b.2 to begin using water again.
(c) Deposits.
(1) Setting of deposit fees. The authority is authorized to establish security deposit fees to be paid for water and sewer service and to collect such fees upon application for service and at such other times as the authority may determine to be necessary. Notice will be sufficiently given to the customer by a publication of deposit fee changes at least two (2) times in consecutive weeks in the official newspaper of Butts County prior to the increase.
(2) Refund of deposits. When a customer moves out of a property, the deposit, less any amount owed, will be refunded to the customer. Also, individual security deposits are also refunded to customers with an excellent payment history after 24 months on the system. Payment history is considered excellent if the customer has had no more than one late penalty during the 24 months. If the customer receives a second late payment penalty during this time frame, the 24 month period will begin again from the date of the last penalty. No interest will apply.
(3) Exemption from deposit. Customers who have been on the authority's system for 24 months or longer, and who have excellent payment history, may be exempted from paying a security deposit if moving from one address to another, or if adding another unit to the system.
(4) Requirement of deposit from landlords under certain circumstances. When rental property service is in the name of the renter and if: a. the property is vacated, b. a new tenant does not immediately move in, and c. the service is shut off at the meter, the property owner will be responsible for the minimum monthly bill, but will not be required to make a deposit. If service is not shut off at the meter, a regular deposit will be required from the property owner.
(d) Tap fees. Tap fees are applied when a new tap must be made in the water main to make the service connection. Tap fees are set by the authority and charged according to the schedule shown in Appendix B.
(e) Meter fees. Meter fees are applied in developments where the developer has previously installed water taps and only a meter installation is required to make the service connection. Meter fees are set by the authority and charged according to the schedule shown in Appendix B.
(f) Payment plans. In cases of extreme financial hardship, the authority manager may give approval for a customer to pay required connection fees over time. The customer must provide documentation of financial need. The maximum extension allowed will be twenty-five percent down with the balance paid in equal payments over six months.
(g) Capital recovery fees. Any person or corporation who ties onto the water system's established service area shall pay a Capital Recovery Fee in the manner and amount established by this ordinance. In all cases, the Capital Recovery Fee must be paid prior to authorization of connection to the water system area in the form of an executed Tap Agreement.
(1) Computation of capital recovery fee. The capital recovery fee assessment shall be in accordance with the fee schedule shown in Appendix A or as otherwise established pursuant to applicable procedures of this ordinance. Any Capital Recovery Fee imposed shall not exceed a project's proportionate share of the cost of system improvements, shall be calculated on the basis of the establishment of service areas, and shall be calculated on the basis of levels of service for public facilities that are the same for existing development as for new growth and development.
(2) Individual fee determination
a. Petition allowed. An applicant for development approval may petition the authority for an individual fee determination of Capital Recovery Fees due for a project.
b. Individual fee calculation study. An applicant electing an individual fee determination shall submit an Individual Fee Calculation Study for the development activity for which service is sought. The Individual Fee Calculation Study shall follow the methodology and format of the current "Water Capital Recovery Fee Report" or, subject to prior approval of the Administrator, such other professionally accepted methodology that identifies a project's proportionate share. The applicant shall attend a pre-application meeting with the Administrator, and no agreement or understanding in regard to data assumptions or methodology shall be binding upon the authority unless specifically agreed to by the authority in writing. The documentation submitted shall show the basis upon which the Individual Fee Calculation was made.
c. Determination time frame. The Administrator shall provide the applicant with the Individual Fee Determination within thirty (30) days after presentation of the Individual Fee Calculation Study.
(3) Changes to proposed development. Not withstanding the issuance of any such certification, any changes in or additions to the proposed development activity different from the development activity identified in the original application shall be subject to increased or additional Capital Recovery Fees to the extent that such changes or additions would have resulted in the determination of a different fee than that assessed from the original application. The additional Capital Recovery Fees shall be based upon the Capital Recovery Fee Schedule in effect at the time of any such change or addition.
(4) Payment of capital recovery fees.
a. Payment required prior to water tap/meter agreement. Any persons required to pay Capital Recovery Fees pursuant to this ordinance shall pay such fees to the authority prior to the issuance of an approved water tap/meter agreement unless the authority has previously approved a Private Development Agreement providing for an alternative method of payment.
b. Additional payment required due to alteration or expansion. Any persons who engage in an alteration or expansion of an existing building or use of land already on the water system, which results in an additional water demand will be required to pay additional assessed Capital Recovery Fees prior to the issuance of a building permit.
c. Fees to be deposited into trust fund. All funds collected pursuant to this ordinance shall be properly identified by the Capital Recovery Fee Service Area from which it was collected and promptly transferred for deposit into the appropriate Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund to be held in separate accounts as provided for in Sec. 90-36.g.10 (Capital Recovery Fee Trust Funds Established) of this ordinance. Funds shall be used solely for the purposes specified in this ordinance.
(5) Use of funds.
a. Funds to be used for system improvements. Funds collected as Capital Recovery Fees shall be used for System Improvements. No funds shall be used for periodic or routine maintenance or for any purpose not in accordance with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 36-71-8. Capital Recovery Fees shall be used exclusively for System Improvements in the Service Area in which the project for which the fees were paid is located. Funds shall be expended in the order in which they are collected.
b. Annual report required. Each fiscal year, the authority's general manager shall present to the authority's board of directors an annual report describing the amount of Capital Recovery Fees collected, encumbered and used during the preceding year. Monies, including any accrued interest, not encumbered in any fiscal year shall be retained in the same Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund(s) until the next fiscal year except as provided in § 90-36.g.8 (Refunds) of this ordinance.
c. Administrative fee. The authority shall be entitled to retain up to three percent (3%) of all Capital Recovery Fees it collects as an administrative fee to offset the costs of administering this ordinance.
d. Fees may be used for debt service. Capital Recovery Fees may be used for the payment of principal and interest on bonds, notes or other financial obligations issued by or on behalf of the authority to finance system improvements.
(6) Credits.
a. Project improvements. No credit shall be given for Project Improvements.
b. System improvements. Credit shall be given for the Present Value of the construction of improvements or contribution or dedication of land or money by a developer or his predecessor in title for System Improvements accepted by the authority in accordance with a Private Development Agreement.
1. A person claiming Credits under a Private Development Agreement shall submit to the Administrator a project description in sufficient detail to allow the Administrator to prepare an engineering and construction cost estimate. A person proposing credit for system improvements shall present cost estimates and property appraisals prepared by duly licensed and qualified professionals to be used by the Administrator in determining the amount of the credit. All construction must be carried out in accordance with applicable authority, county, or state development and design standards. A person seeking Credits under a Private Development Agreement for land dedication shall present the Administrator with property appraisals prepared by qualified professionals and a certified copy of the most recent assessment of the property for tax purposes. However, the authority retains the right to determine the amount to be credited by preparing engineering and construction cost estimates and/or property appraisals for those improvements.
2. Credits must be claimed at the time of the application for water service. Any credit not so claimed shall not be available as to any Capital Recovery Fee owed with respect to water service to that particular property.
3. In the event that a developer contracts with the authority to construct, fund, or contribute System Improvements so that the amount of the Credit created by such construction, funding or contribution is in excess of a particular Capital Recovery Fee which would have been otherwise due and owing, the developer shall be reimbursed for such excess contribution, funding, or contribution from the pool of Capital Recovery Fees paid by the development projects located in the service area which benefit by such improvements.
4. Security in the form of a performance bond, or escrow agreement shall be posted with the authority, made payable to the authority in the amount approved by the Administrator equal to one hundred ten percent (110%) of the full cost of the construction of such improvements. If a facility construction project will not be constructed within one (1) year of acceptance of the offer by the authority, the amount of the security shall be increased by ten percent (10%) compounded, for each year of the life of the security. The security shall be reviewed and approved by the authority's attorney prior to the acceptance of the security by the authority.
c. Credit certificate. Credits shall be represented by a written certificate (the "Credit Certificate") setting forth the name of the person or entity to whom the Credit certificate is issued, the number of the Credit Certificate, and the amount of the credit. The authority shall also maintain a register (the "Credit Certificate Register") which shall set forth the name of the credit holder, the number of the Credit Certificate, and the amount of the credit.
(7) Exemptions.
a. Exempt development types. The following shall be exempted from the payment of Capital Recovery Fees:
1. Alteration or expansion of an existing building or use of land where no additional living units are created, where the use is not changed, and where the Administrator determines that no additional demand will result.
2. The construction of accessory buildings or structures which will not result in additional demand as determined by the Administrator.
3. The replacement of a building or structure that was in place on the effective date of this ordinance, or the replacement of a building or structure that was constructed subsequent thereto and for which the correct Capital Recovery Fee had been paid or otherwise provided for, with a new building or structure of the same use, provided that no additional demand will result as determined by the Administrator.
b. Documentation required for exemption. A person claiming exemptions(s) pursuant to section 90-36.g.7a above shall submit to the Administrator information and documentation sufficient to permit the Administrator to determine whether such exemption claimed is proper, and, if so, the extent of such exemption.
c. Time for exemption application. Exemptions must be applied for at the time of the application for a building permit except in the case of a private development agreement. Any exemptions not so applied for shall be deemed waived.
(8) Refunds. Refunds of impact fees shall be made only in the following instances and in the following manner:
a. Capacity available but service denied. Upon application to the Administrator by the Feepayer, the authority shall refund ninety-seven percent (97%) of the Capital Recovery Fee if capacity is available and service is denied. The authority shall retain three percent (3%) of the fee paid as an administrative fee.
b. Failure to encumber or expend fee when service is not available.
1. Upon application to the Administrator by the Feepayer, the authority shall refund ninety-seven percent (97%) of the Capital Recovery Fee paid and not expended or encumbered if the authority, after collecting the fee when service is not available, has failed to encumber the fee or commence construction within six (6) years from the date the Capital Recovery Fee was paid. The authority shall retain three percent (3%) of the fee paid as an administrative fee. In determining whether capital Recovery Fees have been expended or encumbered, fees shall be considered encumbered on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis.
2. When the right to a refund exists due to a failure to encumber Capital Recovery Fees, the authority shall provided written notice of entitlement to a refund to the Feepayer who paid the Capital Recovery Fee at the address shown on the application for development approval, or to a Feepayer's successor in interest who has give the authority notice of the transfer or assignment of the right or entitlement to a refund and who has provided the authority a mailing address. The authority shall also publish such notice within thirty (30) days of the expiration of the six (6) year period after the date the capital Recovery Fee was paid. The published notice shall contain the heading "Notice of Entitlement to Capital Recovery Fee Refund".
c. Refund application due within one year. A refund application shall be made to the Administrator within one (1) year from the date such refund becomes payable under paragraphs A and B of this section or within one (1) year from the date of publication of the Notice of Entitlement of a Refund under paragraph (b) of this section, whichever is later. Any refund not applied for within said time period shall be deemed waived.
d. Refund documentation required. A refund application shall include information and documentation sufficient to permit the Administrator to determine whether the refund claimed is proper, and if so, the amount of such refund.
e. Accrued Interest to Be Applied. A refund shall include a pro rata share of interest actually earned on the unused or excess impact fee paid.
f. Time period for refunds. All refunds shall be paid within sixty (60) days after the Administrator determines that such refund is due.
(9) Water capital recovery fee service area established. The water system service area consists of all areas of unincorporated Butts County served by the authority. This includes: (1) properties along roadways currently served by the authority's system and (2) any new subdivisions and commercial/industrial developments to be served by connection to the authority's system with new county or private roads.
The area does not include properties served by existing county roads that do not have access to water service. However, once water service from the authority has been available for connection on any of those roads for a period of thirty days, said roads will be included in the service area.
The service area is expected to expand in the future to include any and all additional area served by the water system, with no separate service areas anticipated to be established.
(10) Water capital recovery fee trust fund established.
a. Establishment. There is hereby established a Water Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund.
b. Funds shall be interest bearing. Capital Recovery Fees shall be deposited and maintained in one or more interest bearing accounts. Interest earned on Capital Recovery Fees shall be funds of the account on which it is earned and subject to all restrictions imposed by section 6.4 (Use of Funds) of this ordinance.
(11) Review of fee structure. The Capital Recovery Fee structure shall be reviewed by the authority's board of directors annually. The failure to review such structure shall not invalidate this ordinance.
(12) Administrative appeals.
a. Appealable items. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Administrator with respect to any of the following determinations shall have the right to appeal to the authority's board of directors: (a) the imposition of a Capital Recovery Fee, (b) the amount of a Capital Recovery Fee, (c) the entitlement to and/or the amount of credits to a Capital Recovery Fee, (d) the entitlement to an exemption from a Capital Recovery Fee, and (e) the entitlement to and/or the amount of a refund of a Capital Recovery Fee. Prior to any appeal to the authority's board of directors, the aggrieved party shall file a request for reconsideration with the Administrator, who shall act upon the request within thirty (30) days.
b. Timetable for hearing appeals. All appeals shall be taken within thirty (30) days of the Administrator's decision on the request for reconsideration by filing with the Administrator a notice of appeal specifying the grounds therefor. The authority's board of directors shall establish a date and time for a hearing on the appeal, give due notice thereof to the parties in interest, and decide the same within a reasonable period of time following the hearing. Any party taking an appeal shall have the right to appear at the hearing to present evidence and may be represented by counsel. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the authority's board of directors may take an appeal to the Superior Court of Butts County within thirty (30) days after the decision of the authority is rendered.
c. Payment under protest. A person may pay a Capital Recovery Fee under protest to obtain an approved water tap agreement, and by making such payment shall not be stopped from (a) exercising the right of appeal provided in this section or (b) receiving a refund of any amount as a result of such appeal.
1017:
(a) Reading schedule. The water meter serving the customer's property shall be read on a monthly basis and official records of each reading thereof shall be kept for a minimum period of one (1) year.
(b) Meter designation. Water meters shall be classified as either "active meters", "inactive meters", and "canceled meters". These designations are defined as follows:
(1) Active meters. "Active meters" are defined as meters that are in normal use. All active meters will be charged on a monthly basis.
(2) Inactive meters. "Inactive meters" are defined as meters that are installed where the customer has notified the authority in writing to temporarily terminate service. When it receives such written request, the authority will seal the meter and declare the meter an inactive meter. When no responsible party is available to request inactive meter designation for the customer, the authority may declare the meter inactive. If a customer desires to obtain water services after the meter has been declared inactive, the customer shall pay a re-connection fee as set in the prevailing fee schedule of the authority. In addition, the customer must pay any previous unpaid bills which that customer had through the authority's services prior to obtaining any additional service from the authority. Once the connection fee and any past due bills have been paid, the meter will be re-classified as an active meter as defined above.
(3) Canceled meters. Canceled meters are defined as meters that have not been in use where the customer has notified the authority that no further water service from the authority is desired. The authority may, on its own initiative, declare a meter canceled when water has not been used for a period of twelve (12) months or longer. If a meter is declared a canceled meter, the meter will be removed and the connection sealed. A customer desiring re-connection of a canceled meter shall pay the capital recovery fee, meter fee, and security deposit that is in effect as of the date of application.
1018:
(a) Payment. The customer shall pay promptly on a monthly basis all water registered by the meter serving said property at the rates set by the authority from time to time, which shall include water used, water wasted, or leakage, except for the water that may be traced by the authority to the authority's system. Property owners shall be responsible for any unpaid water bills left by tenants.
(b) Billing Schedule. The authority is authorized to establish billing schedules for payment of water and sewer service.
(c) Billing errors. If the customer believes his/her bill to be in error, this claim must be presented to the authority, or its billing agent, before the bill becomes due. Such claim, if made after the bill has become delinquent, shall not be effective in preventing discontinuance of service as heretofore provided. The customer may pay such bill under protest and said payment shall not prejudice his claim. Any customer who fails to notify the authority in writing within 30 days after the date of said bill of any irregularities or errors that may be in said bill shall waive any right or claim for correction or refund under said bill.
(d) Meter failure. If the seal of a meter is broken by any person other than the authority's representative, or if the meter fails to register correctly, or is stopped for any cause, the customer shall pay an amount which is the average for the three (3) previous months water usage.
(e) Meter testing. The authority will carry out a regular program of meter testing and replacement. In addition, water meters will be tested at the request of the customer.
If the meter is found to be reading at a higher rate than actual flow, no charge will be made. However, if the meter is found to be reading at 101.5% or less, the customer will be required to pay a service fee to be set by the authority.
(f) Meter reading re-checks. The authority may establish and charge a fee for meter reading re-checks except that no fee will be charged for re-checks requested by the customer when the original reading shown appears to have been incorrect.
(g) Credit for excessive leakages. In cases where water is shown to have leaked through a customer's private water piping and has caused billing which is over 20,000 in excess of that customer's average monthly usage over the previous twelve months, the customer will be required to pay only the authority's current cost of water plant operation per 1000 gallons for said usage over 20,000 gallons over the average. In cases of extremely high bills due to such leaks, the authority manager may set up a payment schedule for the customer.
(h) Returned check fee. Customers who make payments with checks which are not covered by sufficient funds will be charged a "returned check fee" as set by the authority. When a customer has written two (2) checks which have been returned for insufficient funds, the authority will accept only cash or money orders for future payment as long as the account remains in that customer's name. This is regardless of who makes the payment on the account.
(i) Water bill payment extensions. Customers will be allowed a maximum of two time extensions per year for payment of water bill. This applies to late payment penalties, warning fees, and reconnect fees.
In Witness Whereof, the partners hereto, acting under the authority of their respective governing bodies, have caused this Contract to be duly executed in two (2) counterparts, each of which shall constitute an original.
1020:
The authority shall have the right from time to time, if necessary, to restrict water to the customer under specific rules and regulations that are contained in its Water Conservation Plan and Drought Contingency Plan, or that may be adopter hereafter by the authority.
The authority shall also restrict water to the customer under the direction and rules of the Environmental Protection Division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources.
1021:
(a) authority's responsibility for line extension. When public funds are available for line extensions, the authority will carry out construction in the order established in a priority road list adopted by the authority. This list shall be based upon a balance of sound engineering and service to a maximum customer base. A current road priority list for line extensions on roads unincorporated Butts County shall be maintained by the authority and made available to the public.
(b) Plans and specifications for construction of water lines. The authority shall have the right to specify the requirements, plans, and specifications for construction of water lines in unincorporated Butts County. All water lines constructed, or paid for, by the authority, any municipality, utility, contractor, consumer, owner, or developer shall be constructed according to the plans and specifications established by the authority for the construction of water lines in Butts County.
No water line shall be covered without first being inspected and approved by the authority. No line shall be put into service without being approved by the authority for disinfection and pressure tightness.
(c) Extensions not initiated by the authority.
(1) Water line extensions to existing residential, industrial, and commercial development. The authority recognizes that areas of pre-existing development may have property owners who desire water service prior to public funds being available for construction. Therefore, on existing public roads, the authority will provide labor and equipment at no charge for line extensions to existing development under the following conditions:
a. Right-of-way. Water lines may only be extended along county roads which have sufficient dedicated right-of-way.
b. Payment for design, materials, blasting. The customer will be required to pay to the authority, prior to the commencement of construction, an amount sufficient to pay for all costs associated with design and materials that are required to build the proposed line and to extend the authority's water main from the existing water main which has sufficient size to service the proposed line.
The cost of the project will be determined by the authority. The authority will provide an initial estimate of cost to the interested parties at no charge. It is immaterial whether the costs for the line are shared equally by the customers or whether one or more property owners or customers pays for the water line extension.
In the event that it becomes apparent to the authority that construction of said line will cost more than the original estimated cost, the authority may terminate work until such time as adequate funds have been placed with the authority.
(2) Authority consideration. The authority's board of directors will consider an application from an existing development, or group of owners of existing development, when the following are provided:
a. Documentation of sufficient right of way and/or easements as required by the county and the authority.
b. A petition of property owners to be served with the signature of all participants, the number of connections to be made for each participant, and an indication of the cost to be borne by each participant.
c. Deposit of the estimated funds for design, materials, and any anticipated blasting.
d. Deposit of the required connection fees for individual customers.
If the request is approved by the authority board, an estimated date of completion will be given to the customer, but a date of completion cannot be guaranteed because of changes in work schedule, weather conditions, equipment breakdown, delays in delivery of materials, improvement of the right of way, or other unpredictable circumstances.
(3) Ownership of lines. All water lines built will become the property of the authority.
(4) Unused funds. Any unused funds provided by the property owners for line construction will be reimbursed by the authority upon completion of construction.
(d) Water line extensions to serve new residential, commercial, and industrial development.
(1) Developer responsible for all costs of extension. This section applies inside new residential subdivisions, industrial sites, and commercial sites and to necessary extensions along existing public roads to reach those sites.
The owner of any new development will be required to pay for labor, materials, design and all other costs of water line extension. At the option of the authority, construction of extensions to and within new development may be done by the authority or by a qualified contractor working for the developer. In any case, line construction must adhere strictly to adopted authority specifications.
(2) Authority consideration. Extensions to new development will be considered under the following conditions:
a. Sufficient dedicated right-of-way must be available along public roads required to access the development.
b. The developer must provide a letter from the Butts County Community Services Department that the property has been approved for the proposed use according to the zoning and development regulations of Butts County.
c. The developer must provide the authority with three (3) copies of a plat or accurate drawing of the property to be served at a format and scale that meets the authority's specifications. Said plats or drawings shall contain the following information:
1. Location of the closest existing water line of the authority which is of sufficient size to serve the property;
2. Location of the existing and proposed roads to serve the property;
3. Exact size, material, and footage of water line that will have to be installed in order to serve the property;
4. Location of all water lines and appurtenances to be constructed in the area to be developed; and
5. Documentation that lines and appurtenances have been sized to meet the specifications the county and the authority for customer demand and fire flows.
d. The developer must document financial ability to pay the cost of construction. If the construction will be provided by the authority, the total cost of the project, as estimated by the authority, must be paid to the authority.
A letter of credit signed by the president of an accredited bank in the State of Georgia will be acceptable in lieu of cash. In the event that it becomes apparent to the authority that construction of said lines will cost more than the original estimated cost, the authority may terminate work until such time as adequate funds have been placed with the authority, or a revised letter of credit with an adequate figure is received.
(3) Construction by authority. Water lines will only be placed within easements established for such purposes, or within right of way lines of streets and roads which have been certified as being part of the public road system of Butts County. An estimated date of completion cannot be guaranteed because of changes in work schedule, weather conditions, equipment breakdown, delays in delivery of materials, improvement of the right of way, or other unpredictable circumstances.
All water lines built are the property of the authority.
Any unused funds deposited by the Developer for the line construction will be reimbursed by the authority upon commencement of water services.
(4) Construction by developer. Lines will normally be allowed to be constructed by the Developer only within the development itself.
During construction, the authority will inspect work as necessary.
Upon completion of construction by the developer, but prior to the initiation of water service the following must be done:
a. The authority will conduct tests to ensure that completed water lines meet authority specifications for pressure, flow and water quality.

The objectives of this article are:
(1) To prevent the introduction of pollutants that will interfere with the operation of the authority's sewer system or otherwise contaminate the natural environment.
(2) To prevent the introduction of inadequately treated pollutants which will pass through either the authority's sewer system or natural environment, thereby polluting receiving waters, lands, or the atmosphere, or otherwise be incompatible with the authority's sewage treatment system.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meaning ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Administrator means the authority's general manager, or his or her designee, responsible for administration of the provisions of Sewerage Capital Recovery Fees.
Authority Board means the board of directors of the Butts County, et al. Water and Sewer Authority.

Any persons who engage in an alteration or expansion of an existing building or use of land already on the sewer system, which results in an additional sewage demand will be required to pay additional assessed Capital Recovery Fees prior to the issuance of a building permit by Butts County or Lamar County.
(c) Fees to be deposited into trust fund. All funds collected pursuant to this ordinance shall be properly identified by the Capital Recovery Fee Service Area from which it was collected and promptly transferred for deposit into the appropriate Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund to be held in separate accounts as provided for in Sec. 90-86 (Capital Recovery Fee Trust Funds Established) of this ordinance. Funds shall be used solely for the purposes specified in this ordinance.
1055:
(a) Funds to be used for system improvements. Funds collected as Capital Recovery Fees shall be used for System Improvements. No funds shall be used for periodic or routine maintenance or for any purpose not in accordance with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 36-71-8. Capital Recovery Fees shall be used exclusively for System Improvements in the Service Area in which the project for which the fees were paid is located. Funds shall be expended in the order in which they are collected.
(b) Annual report required. Each fiscal year, the authority's general manager shall present to the authority's board of directors an annual report describing the amount of Capital Recovery Fees collected, encumbered and used during the preceding year. Monies, including any accrued interest, not encumbered in any fiscal year shall be retained in the same Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund(s) until the next fiscal year except as provided in Sec. 90-84 (Refunds) of this ordinance.
(c) Administrative fee. The authority shall be entitled to retain up to three percent (3%) of all Capital Recovery Fees it collects as an administrative fee to offset the costs of administering this ordinance.
(d) Fees may be used for debt service. Capital Recovery Fees may be used for the payment of principal and interest on bonds, notes or other financial obligations issued by or on behalf of the authority to finance system improvements.
1056:
(a) Project improvements. No credit shall be given for Project Improvements.
(b) System improvements. Credit shall be given for the Present Value of the construction of improvements or contribution or dedication of land or money by a developer or his predecessor in title for System Improvements accepted by the authority in accordance with a Private Development Agreement.
(1) A person claiming Credits under a Private Development Agreement shall submit to the Administrator a project description in sufficient detail to allow the Administrator to prepare an engineering and construction cost estimate. A person proposing credit for system improvements shall present cost estimates and property appraisals prepared by duly licensed and qualified professionals to be used by the Administrator in determining the amount of the credit. All construction must be carried out in accordance with applicable authority, county, or state development and design standards. A person seeking Credits under a Private Development Agreement for land dedication shall present the Administrator with property appraisals prepared by qualified professionals and a certified copy of the most recent assessment of the property for tax purposes. However, the authority retains the right to determine the amount to be credited by preparing engineering and construction cost estimates and/or property appraisals for those improvements.
(2) Credits must be claimed at the time of the application for sewer service. Any credit not so claimed shall not be available as to any Capital Recovery Fee owed with respect to sewer service to that particular property.
(3) In the event that a developer contracts with the authority to construct, fund, or contribute System Improvements so that the amount of the Credit created by such construction, funding or contribution is in excess of a particular Capital Recovery Fee which would have been otherwise due and owing, the developer shall be reimbursed for such excess contribution, funding, or contribution from the pool of Capital Recovery Fees paid by the development projects located in the service area which benefit by such improvements.
(4) Security in the form of a performance bond, or escrow agreement shall be posted with the authority, made payable to the authority in the amount approved by the Administrator equal to one hundred ten percent (110%) of the full cost of the construction of such improvements. If a facility construction project will not be constructed within one (1) year of acceptance of the offer by the authority, the amount of the security shall be increased by ten percent (10%) compounded, for each year of the life of the security. The security shall be reviewed and approved by the authority's attorney prior to the acceptance of the security by the authority.
(c) Credit certificate. Credits shall be represented by a written certificate (the "Credit Certificate") setting forth the name of the person or entity to whom the Credit certificate is issued, the number of the Credit Certificate, and the amount of the credit. The authority shall also maintain a register (the "Credit Certificate Register") which shall set forth the name of the credit holder, the number of the Credit Certificate, and the amount of the credit.
1057:
(a) Exempt development types. The following shall be exempted from the payment of Capital Recovery Fees:
(1) Alteration or expansion of an existing building or use of land where no additional living units are created, where the use is not changed, and where the Administrator determines that no additional demand will result.
(2) The construction of accessory buildings or structures which will not result in additional demand as determined by the Administrator.
(3) The replacement of a building or structure that was in place on the effective date of this ordinance, or the replacement of a building or structure that was constructed subsequent thereto and for which the correct Capital Recovery Fee had been paid or otherwise provided for, with a new building or structure of the same use, provided that no additional demand will result as determined by the Administrator.
(b) Documentation required for exemption. A person claiming exemptions(s) pursuant to section 4.8.1 above shall submit to the Administrator information and documentation sufficient to permit the Administrator to determine whether such exemption claimed is proper, and, if so, the extent of such exemption.
(c) Time for Exemption Application. Exemptions must be applied for at the time of the application for a building permit except in the case of a private development agreement. Any exemptions not so applied for shall be deemed waived.
1058:
Refunds of impact fees shall be made only in the following instances and in the following manner:
(a) Capacity available but service denied. Upon application to the Administrator by the feepayor, the authority shall refund ninety-seven percent (97%) of the Capital Recovery Fee if capacity is available and service is denied. The authority shall retain three percent (3%) of the fee paid as an administrative fee.
(b) Failure to encumber or expend fee when service is not available.
(1) Upon application to the Administrator by the feepayor, the authority shall refund ninety-seven percent (97%) of the Capital Recovery Fee paid and not expended or encumbered if the authority, after collecting the fee when service is not available, has failed to encumber the fee or commence construction within six (6) years from the date the Capital Recovery Fee was paid. The authority shall retain three percent (3%) of the fee paid as an administrative fee. In determining whether capital Recovery Fees have been expended or encumbered, fees shall be considered encumbered on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis.
(2) When the right to a refund exists due to a failure to encumber Capital Recovery Fees, the authority shall provided written notice of entitlement to a refund to the feepayor who paid the Capital Recovery Fee at the address shown on the application for development approval, or to a feepayor's successor in interest who has given the authority notice of the transfer or assignment of the right or entitlement to a refund and who has provided the authority a mailing address. The authority shall also publish such notice within thirty (30) days of the expiration of the six (6) year period after the date the capital Recovery Fee was paid. The published notice shall contain the heading "Notice of Entitlement to Capital Recovery Fee Refund".
(c) Refund application due within one year. A refund application shall be made to the Administrator within one (1) year from the date such refund becomes payable under paragraphs A and B of this section or within one (1) year from the date of publication of the Notice of Entitlement of a Refund under paragraph (b) of this section, whichever is later. Any refund not applied for within said time period shall be deemed waived.
(d) Refund documentation required. A refund application shall include information and documentation sufficient to permit the Administrator to determine whether the refund claimed is proper, and if so, the amount of such refund.
(e) Accrued interest to be applied. A refund shall include a pro rata share of interest actually earned on the unused or excess impact fee paid.
(f) Time period for refunds. All refunds shall be paid within sixty (60) days after the Administrator determines that such refund is due.
1059: The sewer system service area consists of an area in the southwestern part of Butts County and the northeastern part of Lamar County, each of the areas being delimited by the extent of the wastewater collection system. The service area is expected to expand in the future to include any and all additional area served by the wastewater system, with no separate service areas anticipated to be established.
1060:
(a) Establishment. There is hereby established a Wastewater Capital Recovery Fee Trust Fund.
(b) Funds Shall Be Interest Bearing. Capital Recovery Fees shall be deposited and maintained in one or more interest bearing accounts. Interest earned on Capital Recovery Fees shall be funds of the account on which it is earned and subject to all restrictions imposed by section 4.6 (Use of Funds) of this ordinance.
1061: The Capital Recovery Fee structure shall be reviewed by the authority's board of directors annually. The failure to review such structure shall not invalidate this ordinance.
1062:
(a) Appealable Items. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Administrator with respect to any of the following determinations shall have the right to appeal to the authority's board of directors: (a) the imposition of a Capital Recovery Fee, (b) the amount of a Capital Recovery Fee, (c) the entitlement to and/or the amount of credits to a Capital Recovery Fee, (d) the entitlement to an exemption from a Capital Recovery Fee, and (e) the entitlement to and/or the amount of a refund of a Capital Recovery Fee. Prior to any appeal to the authority's board of directors, the aggrieved party shall file a request for reconsideration with the Administrator, who shall act upon the request within thirty (30) days.
(b) Timetable for Hearing Appeals. All appeals shall be taken within thirty (30) days of the Administrator's decision on the request for reconsideration by filing with the Administrator a notice of appeal specifying the grounds therefor. The authority's board of directors shall establish a date and time for a hearing on the appeal, give due notice thereof to the parties in interest, and decide the same within a reasonable period of time following the hearing. Any party taking an appeal shall have the right to appear at the hearing to present evidence and may be represented by counsel. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the authority's board of directors may take an appeal to the Superior Court of Butts County within thirty (30) days after the decision of the authority is rendered.
(c) Payment Under Protest. A person may pay a Capital Recovery Fee under protest to obtain an approved sewer tap agreement, and by making such payment shall not be stopped from (a) exercising the right of appeal provided in this section or (b) receiving a refund of any amount as a result of such appeal.
1065:
If the authority authorizes any customer to discharge industrial wastes into the public sewers, such customer shall be charged and assessed a surcharge in addition to any sewer service charges if these wastes have a concentration greater than the following concentrations, which represent a relatively high strength domestic-type wastewater:
(1) A five-day, 20 degrees Celsius biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of 250 milligrams per liter (mg/l), which is also referred to as parts per million (ppm).
(2) A suspended solids content of 250 mg/l.
(3) For wastewater discharging to a treatment plant where nitrification is required, a total Kjeldahl nitrogen (TKN) and/or ammonia (NH3-N) of 7 mg/l (separately or in combination).
(4) For wastewater discharging to a treatment plant where phosphorous and phosphorous compounds (as P) of 25 mg/l.
Such constituents shall be sampled and analyzed in accordance with Standard Methods or other analytical procedure approved by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency or the regulatory agency of the state having jurisdiction. The surcharge shall be based on an average of at least three 24-hour composite samples (or composite samples during the daily discharge); or based on an average of at least six grab samples taken at different hours of operation over at least a three day period. Where different processes are used or different products are manufactured, the highest strength discharge over a five-day period, as sampled above, shall be used as the basis of the surcharge. The amount of such surcharge, which may be charged and assessed against persons discharging industrial waste into the public sewers, shall reflect the cost incurred by the authority in handling the excess of the previously listed constituents. This surcharge shall include a proportionate share of the operational and maintenance costs and replacement costs on the portions of the plant and affected sewer system and other incidental expenses (monitoring, testing and other).
1066:
When any or all of the total suspended solids, BOD, phosphorous, TKN or ammonia of the wastewater accepted for admission to the authority's sewer system exceeds the values described in subsection 5.1 the excess concentration in any or all, as the case may be, shall be subject to a surcharge on the amount derived in accordance with the following formula:
Amount of surcharge in dollars = (pounds of excess constituent) x (prorated facility replacement cost per excess pound + prorated operational, maintenance and incidental costs per excess pound)
Excess poundage shall be figured as follows:
(Wastewater discharged in gallons × excess concentration in mg/l × 8.34 lbs gallons) divided by 1,000,000.
Example:
1,000,000 gallons of wastewater
250 mg/1 excess BOD (500 mg/l - 250 mg/l)
Then:
Excess poundage | = | 1,000,000 × 250 × 8.34 1,000,000
1067: The rates of surcharges shall be reviewed annually by the authority in order that the factors in Sec. 90-102 of this section may correctly represent current treatment costs and may be modified at any time.
1068: Industrial waste surcharges provided for in this division shall be prepared and rendered with the regular water and sewer bill. The authority's wastewater collection superintendent or other duly authorized employee of the authority shall be permitted to enter upon any properties for the purpose of inspection, observation, measuring, sampling, and testing in accordance with the provisions of this article.
1069: The volume of flow used to compute industrial waste surcharges shall be based upon metered, estimated or prorated water consumption as shown in the records of meter reading maintained by the authority. If a person discharging waste into the public sewer system produces evidence to the authority that a significant portion of the total annual volume of water used for all purposes does not reach the public sewer system, an estimated percentage of total water consumption to be used in computing charges may be agreed upon between the authority and persons discharging industrial waste into the sewer.
1070: The industrial waste of each customer discharging such waste into the public sewer system shall be subject to annual inspection and determination of character and concentration of such waste. Such action may be made more often as may be deemed necessary by the authority. Samples shall be collected in such a manner as to be representative of the actual quality of the waste. The laboratory methods used in examination of the waste shall be those set forth in "Standard Methods."
1071:
If an analysis of waste, determined by the sampling and gauging of waste from a person or industry by the authority is disputed, a program of resampling and gauging, with subsequent chemical determinations, may be instituted as follows:
(1) The person or industrial user interested must submit a request for resampling and gauging of their waste to the authority by letter and bind themselves to bear the expenses incurred by the authority in the resampling and gauging the subsequent chemical determination of the waste.
(2) The chemist or engineer employed by the company or person responsible for the request submitted to the authority must confer with the authority's person in charge of gauging and sampling. They will establish the length of the rerun and the methods to be employed to determine the flow and to sample the flow.
(3) The chemist or engineer engaged by the person or industry may be present during the gauging and sampling operation and also in the laboratory during the determination of the analysis.
(4) The results of the analysis, determined from the quantity and quality of the flow shall be considered by analysis of record.
1074: No unauthorized person shall uncover, make any connections with or opening into, use, alter, or disturb any public sewer appurtenance thereto without first obtaining a written permit from the authority.
1076: All costs and expenses incident to the installation and connection of the building sewer shall be borne by the owner. The owner shall indemnify the authority from any loss or damage that may directly or indirectly be occasioned by the installation of the building sewer.
1077: A separate and independent building sewer shall be provided for each building, except as otherwise approved for and in unusual circumstances, primarily involving existing buildings. A separate and independent building sewer and connection shall be provided for each residential, commercial and industrial business unit of multi-unit building, except as otherwise approved.
1078: Old building sewers may be used in connection with new buildings only when they are found, on examination and test by the authority, to meet all requirements of this article. All costs associated with the examination and test shall be borne by the owner. Capital recovery fees and sewer connection fees shall be paid in accordance with Division 4 (Capital Recovery Fees) of this ordinance.
1079: The size, slope, alignment, materials of construction, and the methods to be used in construction of a building sewer shall conform to the requirements of the building and plumbing code of Butts County. However, in no event shall the diameter of the building sewer be less than four inches. The slope of such four-inch pipe shall not be less than one-eighth inch per foot.
1080: Whenever possible, the building sewer shall be brought to the building at an elevation below the basement floor. No building sewer shall be laid parallel to or within three feet of any bearing wall, which might thereby be weakened. The depth shall be sufficient to afford protection from the front. The building sewer shall be laid at uniform grade and in straight alignment insofar as possible. Changes in direction shall be made only with properly curved pipe and fittings.
1081: In all buildings in which any building drain is too low to permit gravity flow to the public sewer, sanitary sewage carried by such drain shall be lifted by approved means and discharged to the building sewer.
1082: All excavations required for the installation of a building sewer shall be open trench work unless otherwise approved by the authority. Pipelaying and backfilling shall be performed in a manner approved by the authority.
1083: All joints and connections shall be made gas-tight and watertight.
1084: Material for factory applied joints on sewer pipe shall be the latest approved standard, and manufactured by the pipe manufacturer or approved equal. When jointing sewer pipe, the joint surfaces and pipe interior shall be wiped free of dirt, dust, gravel, or other foreign materials and connected in accordance with manufacturer's recommendations or as otherwise approved by the authority.
1085: Connection of a building sewer into the public sewer shall be made at the wye branch, if such branch is available at a suitable location. If the public sewer is 12 inches in diameter, or less, and a wye is not available, the authority shall, at the expense of the owner, install a wye branch in the public sewer at the location determined by the authority. When the public sewer is greater than 12 inches in diameter, and no approved wye branch is available, the authority shall, at the expense of the owner, cut a hole into the public sewer, with entry in the downstream direction at an angle of about 45 degrees, and install a 45-degree bend with the spigot end cut so as not to extend past the inner surface of the public sewer. The invert of the building sewer at the point of connection shall be at the same or at a higher elevation than the invert of the public sewer. A smooth, neat joint shall be made, and the connection made secure and watertight by encasement in concrete. Special fittings may be used for the connection only when approved by the authority.
1086: All excavations for building sewer installation shall be properly guarded with barricades and lights so as to protect the public from hazard. Streets, sidewalks, parkways and other public property disturbed by the work shall be restored in a manner satisfactory to the authority.
1087: All persons installing sewer service connections for hire in the Butts County shall, before cutting any street, sidewalk or public property, obtain a permit from the county for the cutting of any streets, sidewalks or public property as per Butts County's ordinance for Utility Construction on Public Roads (Article 3, Division 2, Permits).
1088: All building sewers and connections, to the authority's collector line, shall be the responsibility and property of the landowner. The authority shall not have ownership for the building sewers and connections nor responsibility for maintenance of the building sewers and connections.
1089: All plumbing shall be in accordance with applicable Butts County and state codes and requirements and shall be subject to inspection by Butts County.
1090: The authority may from time to time enact separate technical, construction and other rules and regulations for building sewers and connections to supplement or clarify the requirements of this article. Where technical and construction requirements are not otherwise covered in this article, appropriate specifications or standards of the American Society for Testing Materials (ASTM) or the Water Pollution Control Federation (WPCF) Manual of Practice No. 9 shall apply, unless otherwise covered by supplementary rules and regulations of the authority.
1091: All building sewers and connections must be inspected and approved and all applicable fees/charges paid before wastewater can be discharged to any authority sewer.
1094: No person or group not directly tied into the authority's sewage collection system as an authorized customer shall discharge or cause to be discharged any material into the sanitary sewer system of the authority without prior approval of the authority. The authority may accept leachate at its sewerage treatment facilities from other EPD or EPA permitted facilities, EPD or EPA permitted landfills, or licensed septic pumping companies. The authority shall have the right to set the fee for this service.
1095: Any person constructing project sewer improvements shall submit plans and specifications to and obtain approval from the authority before construction is started. The authority may also establish design and construction requirements and specifications that must be met before issuing approval. Development plans shall be prepared by a state registered engineer and shall be subject to any necessary approvals by state and local agencies prior to approval by the authority. The authority reserves the right to inspect construction during progress and perform tests upon completion, prior to acceptance. Any easements and real estate associated with the sewer systems (i.e., sewer line easements across private property and sewage pumping station property) shall be conveyed to the authority for ownership and/or usage in a legal manner acceptable to the authority.
1096: Prior to any sewer systems being placed in use, a final inspection of the system must be conducted, by the authority. If such inspection shows any irregularities or failure to comply with approved plan and specifications, the contractor, landowner or developer shall make, all corrections at their own expense.
1097: Prior to any project sewer improvements being placed in use, the owner of the property shall convey to the authority, the sewer lines and any appurtenances required by the authority, free and clear of any encumbrance, together with an easement of sufficient width as required by the authority for the maintenance and repair of the sewer lines or appurtenance thereto.
1098: For project improvements the owner or developer shall have any necessary plats prepared at his/her own expense by a registered land surveyor or registered engineer authorized to do business in the state. The plats shall be in recordable form properly describing adequate easements upon which any public sewer system is to be located. The plats shall be delivered to the authority for review and acceptance.
1099: All costs and expenses for the construction of the project sewer improvements shall be borne by the property owner. The property owner shall indemnify the authority from any and all loss or damage including, but not limited to, attorney's fees, court costs, expert witness fees, engineering fees and judgments that it incurs which may be directly or indirectly occasioned by the installation of the sewer system.
1102:
No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged any drainage such as stormwater, groundwater, roof runoff or subsurface drainage to any sewer. Connection, directly or indirectly, to roof downspouts, exterior foundation drains, area drains, or other sources of surface runoff is not permitted to a building drain or building sewer connected to a public sanitary sewer. Existing connections of such items to a building sewer shall be disconnected at no expense to the authority when it is determined that the building sewer is connected to the public sewer system.
Unpolluted industrial cooling water or process water may be discharged, on approval of the authority, to a sanitary sewer, if the water otherwise meets the requirements and specifications of this article.
1103: No unauthorized person shall uncover, make any connection with or open, use, alter or disturb any public sanitary sewer or appurtenance.
1104:
No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged any of the following described waters, wastes, substances or materials to any public sewers:
(1) Any gasoline, benzene, naphtha, fuel oil, or other flammable or explosive liquid, solid or gas.
(2) Any waters containing toxic or poisonous solids, liquids, or gases in sufficient quantity, either singly or by interaction with other substances, to injure or interfere with any waste treatment process, constitute a hazard to humans or animals, create a public nuisance, or create any hazard in the receiving waters of the wastewater treatment plant.
(3) Any waters or wastes having a pH lower than 6.0 or a pH in excess of 9.0, or having any other corrosive property capable of causing damage or hazard to structures, equipment, and personnel .
(4) Solid or viscous substances in quantities of such size capable of causing obstruction to the flow in sewers, or other interference with the proper operation of the wastewater facilities such as, but not limited to, ashes, bones, cinders, sand, mud, straw shavings, metal, glass, rags, feathers, tar, plastics, wood, un-ground garbage, whole blood, paunch manure, hair and fleshing, entrails, paper dishes, cups, milk containers, etc., either whole or ground by garbage grinders (size may not be greater than one-half inch in any dimension).
(5) Wastes at a flow rate and/or pollutant discharge rate which is excessive over relatively short time periods so that there is a treatment process upset and subsequent loss of treatment efficiency.
(6) Any other circumstances that from time to time may be listed by the authority.
1105:
The following described substances, materials, waters, or waste shall be limited in discharges to public sanitary sewers to concentrations or quantities which will not harm either the sewers, wastewater treatment process or equipment, will not have any adverse effect on the receiving stream or land, and will not otherwise endanger lives, limb, public property or constitute a nuisance.
The authority may set limitations lower than the limitations established in the regulations in this section if, in its opinion, such more severe limitations are necessary to meet the objectives of this section. In forming its opinion as to the acceptability, the authority will give consideration to such factors as the quantity of subject waste in relation to flows and velocities in the sewers, materials or construction of the sewer; the wastewater treatment process employed and wastewater discharge requirements; capacity of the wastewater treatment plant; degree of treatability of the waste in the wastewater treatment plant; and the toxicity of the pollutant, its persistence, degradability and other pertinent factors. The limitations or restrictions on materials or characteristics of waste or wastewaters discharged to the sanitary sewer which shall not be violated without approval of the authority are as follows:
(1) Any liquid or vapor having a temperature higher than 150 degrees Fahrenheit (65 degrees Celsius).
(2) Wastewater containing more than 25 milligrams per liter of petroleum oil, nonbiodegradable cutting oils, or product of mineral oil origin.
(3) Wastewater from industrial plants containing oils, fats, or grease in excess of 100 milligrams per liter.
(4) Any garbage that has not been properly shredded (any dimension greater than one half inch). Garbage grinders may be connected to sanitary sewers from homes, hotels, institutions, restaurants, hospitals, catering establishments, or similar places where garbage originates from the preparation of food in kitchens for the purpose of consumption on the premises or when served by caterers.
(5) Any waters or wastes containing the following constituents at a concentration greater than the following fixed upper limits measured in parts per million by weight:
